summary: A survey of concentration camps from Andrew Jackson's Indian removal and Valeriano Weyler's 1896 Cuban reconcentration camps through the Boer War, the Armenian genocide and Nazi Germany to the 2018 US family separations.

evidence.note: Jackson segment starts with his 1812 militia command and the Red Stick War
Weyler biography begins: born 1838 in Mallorca
Weyler proposes forced relocation into camps in Cuba, 1896
British adopt camps in the Boer War under Kitchener
Armenian deportees die in an open-air camp near Deir ez-Zor in the Syrian desert
Nazi camps framed as continuation; Hitler and Goering cite Boer and US precedents
Briggs Plan new villages in Malaya described at length
2018 US border family separations and tender-age shelters for children
Romanian orphanage study used only as a comparison, not counted in span

notes: No theme for detention camps specifically; policing-incarceration is closest (detention). The transcript gives Weyler's death as 1932; standard sources say 1930. Lifespan follows the transcript per the prompt. Hadrian's Wall camps are a passing mention, so covered_span starts with the 1812 Red Stick War. Setting drops PH, VN, GB, DZ for space.
